claims.claim: Judges 9:6 reports Shechem and Beth-millo making Abimelech king
claims.evidence: Judges 9:6 (Hebrew Bible, Judges 1–21, Masoretic text, read in full in Hebrew and JPS English via Mechon Mamre). Textual description only; the narrated event is not externally corroborated.

claims.claim: Fortress-temple and destruction phases at Tell Balata/Shechem are real archaeological contexts; association with Abimelech and Baal-berith is interpretive, not demonstrated.
claims.evidence: Judges 9:4 (Hebrew Bible, Judges 1–21, Masoretic text, read in full in Hebrew and JPS English via Mechon Mamre). The excavated fortress-temple at Tell Balata/Shechem is a real archaeological context (Shechem overview, verified, read in full); the association with Baal-berith is interpretive, not demonstrated. The ABR essay (verified, full read) proposes the association; it is cited only for the association as proposed, not as claim support. No positive Abimelech-event link to any Shechem layer is asserted.

claims.claim: Fortress-temple and destruction phases at Tell Balata/Shechem are real archaeological contexts; association with a specific burning is interpretive, not demonstrated.
claims.evidence: Judges 9:46 (Hebrew Bible, Judges 1–21, Masoretic text, read in full in Hebrew and JPS English via Mechon Mamre). The excavated fortress-temple at Tell Balata/Shechem is a real archaeological context (Shechem overview, verified, read in full); the association with a specific burning is interpretive, not demonstrated. No conflagration contemporary with the temple's last days left evidence in the temple vicinity; a site-wide burning is not a temple burning, and no evidence ties a fire in the temple vicinity to Judges 9. No positive Abimelech-event link to any Shechem layer is asserted.

claims.claim: Abimelech’s death follows an upper millstone dropped by a woman
claims.evidence: Judges 9:53–54 (Hebrew Bible, Judges 1–21, Masoretic text, read in full in Hebrew and JPS English via Mechon Mamre). Textual description only; the narrated event is not externally corroborated. A narrative reversal, not an excavated assassination.

JCL-06-002 SPLIT into two claims (verification report coverage-and-discrepancy.md §3: the registry passage "Judges 9:4,46" uses discontinuous notation and must be split (9:4 + 9:46) or narrowed if built — one claim spanning 9:4–46 would swallow vv. 7–45): clm-jud-06-002 is grounded in Judges 9:4 (association with Abimelech and Baal-berith is interpretive, not demonstrated) and clm-jud-06-003 in Judges 9:46 (association with a specific burning is interpretive, not demonstrated); together they preserve all three limbs of the registry's corrected wording. JADD-007 (ACCEPT, additional-items-review.md §JADD-007) is a methodological rule, not a factual claim, so it is not a claim in this JSON; it is the basis for the split and the narrowed wording, and its two objects (Judges 9:4–6; 9:46–49) are kept separate in this article, never built as one continuous passage. No internal research IDs (JCL-/JADD-) appear in the reader-facing prose, and the prose is kept precise to what the claims state (no positive Abimelech-event link to any Shechem layer is asserted anywhere).
